name: Zionism
summary: Zionism is the nationalist movement holding that Jews are a people entitled to self-determination in a state of their own in the Land of Israel. It organized Jewish immigration and settlement, revived Hebrew and Jewish national culture, and founded the State of Israel in 1948; since then it has centered on sustaining Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, encouraging immigration, and securing it militarily. Its strands range from socialist to free-market and from secular to religious, so it has little common economic program.
scope: The shared core of mainstream Zionism as set out in Herzl's The Jewish State (1896), the Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel (1948) and the World Zionist Organization's Jerusalem Program, with Jabotinsky's Iron Wall for the security doctrine common to the mainstream, and contemporary attitudes drawn from Pew's survey of Israeli Jews. Economic and social questions where Labor, General, Revisionist and Religious Zionism differ are answered as split. Separate profiles exist for strands such as Labor Zionism; Christian Zionism, post-Zionism and anti-Zionist positions are excluded.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience, which punishing a person for leaving a religion would contradict.

bound-labor.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of social and political rights to all inhabitants, which excludes legally binding farmers to estates.

clerical-rule.rationale: Herzl writes "Shall we end by having a theocracy? No, indeed" and says priests will be kept "within the confines of their temples" and must not interfere in the administration of the State.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Declaration provides that the Constitution "shall be adopted by the Elected Constituent Assembly" and that regular authorities follow it.

culture-before-state.rationale: Herzl's book puts the founding of the state first, while Ahad Ha'am argues for a gradual cultural settlement rather than an independent State; the movement's own texts differ, in words.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration says the State "will be open for Jewish immigration and for the Ingathering of the Exiles", and the WZO mission statement commits it to "encouraging the return to Zion".

direct-votes.rationale: Herzl writes that he holds "a settling of questions by the referendum to be an unsatisfactory procedure".

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Declaration promises equal social and political rights irrespective of sex, which a law assigning different public roles by sex would contradict.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Herzl's Jewish State is to be a neutral State whose existence Europe guarantees, rather than a party to a military alliance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration promises "complete equality of social and political rights to all its inhabitants irrespective of religion, race or sex".

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Declaration states as fact "the massacre of millions of Jews in Europe" and cites it as showing the urgency of a Jewish state.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Declaration makes the state open to the Ingathering of the Exiles, while Ahad Ha'am wants a homeland settlement that becomes the spiritual centre sending its spirit out to the diaspora communities; the sources of the movement point both ways, in words.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Declaration says the Land of Israel is where the Jewish people's "spiritual, religious and political identity was shaped" and that they never ceased to pray and hope for their return.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Declaration grounds the state in a collective right of the Jewish people as a nation, "like all other nations".

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Declaration proclaims "the establishment of a Jewish State in Eretz-Israel", Herzl's book argues for the same state, and the Basel Program aims at a legally assured home in Eretz Yisrael.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Herzl says Jews cannot converse in Hebrew, that "Switzerland affords a conclusive proof of the possibility of a federation of tongues", and that the Jews are bound together by the faith of their fathers, not by a language.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Encyclopaedia Judaica records a continuing battle inside the movement between Socialist Zionism and General Zionists who held that free enterprise had to be released; the movement's account of itself holds both sides.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Herzl writes that army and priesthood "must not interfere in the administration of the State", and the army is kept within its barracks.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Declaration calls statehood "the natural right of the Jewish people to be masters of their own fate, like all other nations, in their own sovereign State".

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Declaration says the State "will foster the development of the country for the benefit of all its inhabitants", more than protection from violence.

people-in-arms.rationale: Herzl speaks of "our professional army", to be kept within the confines of its barracks, so the state he describes keeps a professional army.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Jerusalem Program's fourth foundation is ensuring the future and distinctiveness of the Jewish people through Jewish, Hebrew and Zionist education and its spiritual and cultural values.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: The Declaration opens the State to the Ingathering of the Exiles and appeals to the Jewish people in the Diaspora to join the tasks of immigration, and the WZO commits itself to encouraging the return to Zion.

public-ownership.rationale: The Encyclopaedia Judaica records Socialist Zionists striving for a socialist, economically egalitarian society against General Zionists who insisted on free enterprise, a continuing battle within the movement.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of political rights irrespective of religion and race, which excludes a vote limited to one ethnic group.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration promises equal social and political rights irrespective of race; enforced segregation of public life could not be true alongside it.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Declaration counts the revival of Hebrew among the achievements of the return and the Encyclopaedia Judaica treats it as part of the movement; Herzl in 1896 left the national language open, so this is the later, sustained position.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Herzl argues that Jews everywhere have honestly tried to merge into surrounding communities in vain, and that the Jewish question is a national question solved by a Jewish state, not by equal rights where Jews live.

state-harmful.rationale: Creating a sovereign Jewish state is the movement's aim in Herzl's book and the Declaration.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Herzl says every man will be free in his faith or his disbelief, and the Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience; a state campaign for atheism contradicts both.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Herzl proposes that the Jewish State, "as a neutral State", remain in contact with all Europe under a European guarantee of its existence, which keeps it out of rival blocs.

total-state.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion, conscience, language, education and culture, so a state directing every area of life contradicts it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Declaration traces the people from their ancient statehood through the Dispersion, in which they "kept faith" with the land, to the present return.

unions-good.rationale: The Encyclopaedia Judaica records the Histadrut union federation of the Socialist Zionists and the Revisionists' charge that it used its power for its own dominance, a continuing dispute within the movement.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience and equality irrespective of sex; a legal duty on women to cover fully contradicts both.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of social and political rights irrespective of sex, which includes the vote.

missingStatements.text: The Jewish people have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the movement's founding aim, stated by Herzl and enacted in the 1948 Declaration.

missingStatements.text: Jews from anywhere in the world should have the right to immigrate to Israel and become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: Encouraging aliyah and the ingathering of exiles is a listed foundation of Zionism, distinct from immigration policy in general.

missingStatements.text: A people dispersed in exile should return to and rebuild its ancestral homeland.
missingStatements.rationale: Zionism treats diaspora life as something to end through return to the Land of Israel, in a general form other diaspora nationalisms could also answer.

missingStatements.text: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should be revived as the language of the state.
missingStatements.rationale: The revival of Hebrew was a central Zionist project, endorsed by the movement in 1913 and kept in the Jerusalem Program's commitment to Hebrew education.

notes: Zionism is a family whose economic and social views follow its sub-strands, so many answers are 0 at low confidence and the profile may fail the inclusion check. Pew surveys Israeli Jews, a population that includes non-Zionists, and is used only as a proxy for contemporary adherents. Critics describe Zionism as ethnic nationalist or settler colonial, which Wikipedia reports alongside adherents' self-description as a national liberation movement.
